newsitem.title: UK: Barclays drops after low-end profits.
newsitem.headline: Barclays drops after low-end profits.

text.p: Shares in Barclays Plc fell sharply in early trading on Tuesday after the banking group posted 1996 profits at the low end of forecasts.
The stock, down 16-1/2p on Monday from Friday's record close of 12.16 stg, was down 33p at 11.66-1/2 by 0811 GMT.

Barclays' pre-tax profit rose 13 percent to 2.36 billion stg, including an exceptional 70 million gain on disposals, with operating profit at its investment banking unit BZW down 29 percent to 204 million stg.
Analyst forecasts for group pre-tax profits had mostly been in a range between 2.33 billion stg and 2.45 billion.
Yet Barclays raised its dividend 21 percent to 31.5p and said it would return 500 million stg to shareholders in the next twelve months.

"The results were very disappointing and there will be some downgrades as a result," said one head of equity sales. "The trials and tribulations at the investment banking arm look as if they will probably be continuing into the next year."
Elsewhere in the banking sector National Westminster Bank Plc, also heavily exposed to investment banking, fell 12p to 822-1/2.

Other bank stocks were also dragged lower with Lloyds TSB Plc down 2p at 516-1/2, Royal Bank of Scotland Plc down 8p at 612-1/2 and Abbey National Plc down 5p at 780. By 0828 GMT Barclays was down 43-1/2p at 11.56 stg.
